parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A lepton is an example of a fundamental particle.

State what is meant by fundamental particle.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A lambda particle $\Lambda^0$ is a hadron that consists of an up ($u$) quark, a down ($d$) quark and a strange ($s$) quark.

Show that the charge on the $\Lambda^0$ particle is zero.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.part_stem:
The $\Lambda^0$ particle is unstable. It can decay into a neutron ($n$) and a pion ($\pi^0$) as shown by
$$\Lambda^0 \rightarrow n + \pi^0.$$
The $\pi^0$ particle consists of an up quark and an up antiquark.
parts.text: Compare the properties of an up quark and an up antiquark.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the neutron is classed as a baryon and the $\pi^0$ particle is classed as a meson.
